item.title: Cristiano Ronaldo announces international retirement
item.description: The international higlight of Ronaldo's career came when Portugal won the Euro 2016 title (PATRICIA DE MELO MOREIRA) Portuguese football legend Cristiano Ronaldo announced on Thursday he was retiring from international football at the age of 41. Ronaldo made his debut for Portugal in 2003 and went on to play a world record 234 times for his country, scoring 146 goals. But the forward's powers have been waning in recent years and he fell out with national coach Jorge Jesus last month after refusing to play him in a Nations League match. Ronaldo immediately left the team camp and was handed a 30-day suspension. He apologised and it was rumoured he intended to return to the international fold, but on Thursday the five-time winner of the Ballon d'Or released a video on his Instagram account in which he said he had played his last match for Portugal. "To the Portuguese people, the day has come for me to hand back the number seven shirt of our national team," Ronaldo said, as images of his career were played. "I never felt it belonged to me alone, but for 23 years I had the privilege and the responsibility of wearing it, defending it and carrying it with me into stadiums all around the world. "Today the time has come to pass it on to the future. It was not an easy decision, because some decisions are not made with the mind alone -- they are also made with the heart. "A journey that began in August 2003 and changed my life forever has come to an end," he added. - 'Will stay with me forever' - The Portuguese Football Federation said it would organise a "fitting tribute" to Ronaldo's "immense career". Ronaldo will continue to play for his current club in Saudi Arabia, Al-Nassr, where he is under contract until June 2027. In the highlight of his international career, Ronaldo won the European Championship with Portugal in 2016 in France, although he had to leave the field during the final with an injury. "I won Euro 2016 and, for me, that's just as important as the World Cup. It will stay with me forever," he recalled. At this year's World Cup in the United States, Canada and Mexico, he scored three goals but Portugal were knocked out in the last 16 by eventual winners Spain. In a notorious moment at a previous World Cup, a 21-year-old Ronaldo was caught by TV cameras winking at his bench after appearing to exhort the referee to send off his then Manchester United teammate Wayne Rooney as Portugal faced England in the 2006 quarter-finals in Germany. Rooney was red-carded and Ronaldo scored the winning spot kick in the penalty shootout to send Portugal into the semi-finals where they lost to Zinedine Zidane's France. His departure from the international stage follows that of his long-term rival, Lionel Messi, who played his final match for Argentina last month. obo/gj/iwd

item.title: Sweet Seventeen: Roma’s Unbeaten Streak in Serie A Continues
item.description: MANCHESTER, ENGLAND - NOVEMBER 3: Matias Soule of AS Roma celebrates scoring the opening goal during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD4 match between Manchester United and AS Roma at Old Trafford on November 3, 2026 in Manchester, United Kingdom. (Photo by Marc Atkins/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Giallorossi have not lost in Serie A since April 5 and aim to extend their unbeaten run next weekend. Can they break a Roman record this season? A 5-2 loss to Inter in April was the last time AS Roma tasted defeat in Italy. Since then, Gasperini’s boys have gone unbeaten in seventeen games, winning thirteen and drawing four. That’s 43 points out of a possible 51. Now, I’m no math professor, but that’s a damn good score. Even those draws came against tough opponents: Atalanta, Inter, Como, and Napoli. The days when Roma stumbled against Pisa, Cagliari, Parma, or Lecce are long gone. Gasperini has built a machine and made them a force to be reckoned with. What’s even more impressive is the number of goals scored in that same time frame: 45 in 17 games. Malen, of course, is the biggest contributor, but the danger comes from everywhere: Cristante, Ndicka, Mancini, Koné, Hermoso, Rensch, Wesley, Mora, Lulli, Castro, Pisilli; young or old, defender, wingback, or midfielder. Left or right side. Not a single outfield position went without scoring in those 17 games. Kudos to Gasperini, of course. There’s been a big change in mentality, and we’re finally seeing the fluid ‘Gaspball’ we all wanted. This group seems truly united and never gives up. The only downside so far is those pesky second-half goals Roma always concede around the 45’-50’ mark. Then again, who cares about a clean sheet when you always score two or three more goals than your opponent? Give the people some entertainment (cue Russell Crowe screaming at the Colosseo). People also love records. Gasperini has already surpassed Rudi Garcia’s 16-game unbeaten run from 2014-2015. Next up is the 19-game record, set by three Roma teams: 1984 (Eriksson and Liedholm), 2013 (Andreazzoli and Garcia), and 2024-2025 (Ranieri). The best result? Liedholm’s 1980-1981 team, which went 30 games without a loss. Can Gasperini really make history this season? But first things first: surpassing that 19-game unbeaten run looks achievable. The Giallorossi have a couple of winnable games (Sassuolo, Parma, Monza) coming up before the December 13 derby, which is shaping up to be a true Scudetto clash. Who would’ve predicted that in August? To end, here’s a little curiosity from Roma’s previous four games: two goals vs Genoa, three vs Napoli, four vs Cagliari, and last weekend, five against Udinese. Anybody want to bet on a 6-0 win vs Sassuolo this weekend? {Editors note: This was written prior to Tuesday’s loss in Manchester}

item.title: How young can a Formula 1 world champion actually be?
item.description: Motorsport photo Kimi Antonelli became Formula 1 world champion in 2026 at 20 years and 68 days old, breaking Sebastian Vettel 's previous age record by more than three years. But does that make Antonelli the youngest Formula 1 world champion of all time? So far yes, but there is room for someone to come and usurp the Italian. But how young can a Formula 1 world champion actually be, and what are the chances of Antonelli losing his age record to an even younger driver? Part of the answer can be found in Appendix L of the FIA's International Sporting Code. Section 13.1 ("Qualifications for the full Super Licence"), Article 13.1.2, states: "The driver must be at least 18 years old at the start of the event of his first F1 competition." Driving in Formula 1 at 17: Theoretically possible However, that does not mean only drivers aged 18 or over are allowed to compete in Formula 1. Article 13.1.2 also includes an exception, introduced in 2024, which reads: "At the sole discretion of the FIA, a driver judged to have recently and consistently demonstrated outstanding ability and maturity in single-seater formula car competition may be granted a Super Licence at the age of 17 years old." In theory, then, a 17-year-old could become Formula 1 world champion and beat Antonelli's age record by more than two years – provided they managed to win the title in their very first F1 season. Under-18s in Formula 1 There has already been a 17-year-old Formula 1 driver: Max Verstappen was just 17 years and 166 days old when he made his debut in Australia in 2015, making him the youngest driver in Formula 1 history. Verstappen had already completed his first Formula 1 test runs in 2014 at the age of 16. Later that year, shortly after his 17th birthday, he made his first appearance at a Formula 1 race weekend as a Friday practice driver. Franz Tost, Team Principal, Toro Rosso, and Max Verstappen, Toro Rosso Franz Tost, Team Principal, Toro Rosso, and Max Verstappen, Toro Rosso But Verstappen's remarkably early F1 debut had consequences: The FIA tightened its Super Licence requirements and raised the minimum age to 18 from 2016. Young drivers were also required to have competed in single-seater championships for at least two years and accumulated 40 Super Licence points - Verstappen would not have met those criteria. Following the introduction of the age exemption, Antonelli (2024) and Arvid Lindblad (2025) both received their Super Licences at the age of 17. However, both were over 18 by the time they made their Grand Prix debuts – as was Lance Stroll , who debuted in 2017 at the age of 18 years and 148 days, making him the second-youngest Formula 1 driver after Verstappen. In theory, Antonelli's age record could therefore be broken one day. But to achieve that, a driver would probably have to become world champion in their first or second season. How likely is that? item.title: ‘Just an excuse’ – Seattle Seahawks fans share Sam Darnold theory after injury update
item.description: Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images Mike Macdonald revealed that quarterback Sam Darnold will not play this weekend for the Seattle Seahawks against the Arizona Cardinals due to a quad injury. Darnold ended the game on Monday against the Chicago Bears without any apparent injury issues, but Macdonald has revealed news of a quad injury and a cracked rib after Seattle’s crushing loss at Lumen Field. Drew Lock, who is also battling his own fitness issue, will start the game on Sunday against their NFC West rivals. Lock has already beaten the Cardinals this season after stepping in for Darnold following his previous injury earlier in the season. However, there are a number of Seahawks fans who feel as if there may be more to Darnold not playing this weekend, despite Macdonald saying the QB had suffered two separate injuries. Seattle Seahawks fans think Sam Darnold has been soft-benched After winning the Super Bowl in February, Darnold has entered the 2026 season in pretty dreadful form. Since returning from his opening-day injury, Darnold has thrown at least one interception in all six of his games for Seattle. This has led to some fans feeling as if he is being taken out of the firing line this weekend. ‘Basically a soft benching for Darnold,’ replied one Seahawks fan on X after hearing the news. ‘There’s a real possibility Sam Darnold might’ve played his last game last week. This is a soft benching,’ one fan even suggested. Darnold has thrown 10 touchdowns this season and nine interceptions, with games against the Washington Commanders, San Francisco 49ers and Denver Broncos being lost due to the number of turnovers on offense. ‘The classic fake injury soft benching,’ replied another. ‘There’s no way this isn’t just an excuse to bench him right?’ added one fan. Although Darnold has been far from his best this season, a game against the Cardinals would surely be the perfect opportunity for him and the Seahawks to get their season back on track with a strong offensive showing. Yet some fans still think that Darnold is being made to sit this one out due to his poor form. ‘Soft benching, thank you, Mike,’ one happy Seahawks fan said. ‘A sore thigh sounds like a polite demotion,’ replied another. item.title: NCAA men's golf fall awards: Best team, MVP, most exciting tournament
item.description: The fall season in NCAA men's golf is in the books and the early signing period is fast approaching, so what better time than to hand out some fall awards? BEST TEAM: Auburn. Though Oklahoma State is ranked No. 1 in the country, the third-ranked Tigers are 3-0 against the Cowboys. Auburn was 13 shots better at Colonial, where it was runner-up, and beat Oklahoma State twice at the East Lake Cup, one of the Tigers’ three tournament titles this fall. Logan Reilly has continued to elevate his game alongside Walker Cupper Josiah Gilbert while Billy Davis and Alex Holder have become contributors. If Jake Albert can fully shake off his early struggles, Auburn will be favored to win a third NCAA title in four years. CARLSBAD, CALIFORNIA - MAY 25: Max Herendeen of the Illinois Fighting Illini reacts to a chip during the third round of the Division I Men’s Golf Championship held at the Omni La Costa Resort & Spa on May 25, 2025 in Carlsbad, California. (Photo by Tyler McFarland/NCAA Photos via Getty Images) NCAA Photos via Getty Images MOST VALUABLE PLAYER: Max Herendeen, Illinois. Always a tough decision, but it’s made easier when the nation’s top-ranked player is the only top-50 player on the ninth-ranked team in the country. Herendeen’s importance to the Illini, of course, was already known; when he finished outside the top 35 five times last spring while failing to qualify for a tournament that he ended up winning, Illinois sputtered, losing the Big Ten Championship and failing to advance through NCAA regionals. But with Herendeen no longer affected by the pressures of being a world-class player, he’s enjoying some of his best golf yet – win, two more top-3s and nothing worse than T-15 in four fall starts. With mid-majors such as East Tennessee State, Santa Clara and Liberty all in the top 30, I’m still going with the Huskies, who are ranked No. 18 in Thomas Sutton’s first season as head coach. Coming off two straight seasons in which Washington finished below .500, there were little expectations for this program out of the gates. But the Huskies started the fall with an impressive third at Sahalee and then won the St. Mary’s Invitational to cap the semester. BREAKOUT INDIVIDUAL: Johnnie Clark, New Mexico. item.title: Le Havre not in contact with Antoine Kombouaré
item.description: Le Havre not in contact with Antoine Kombouaré Le Havre AC are not in contact with former FC Nantes and Paris FC manager Antoine Kombouaré, as per a report from RMC Sport . He had been strongly linked with the vacancy at the Normand club. It had been reported by Paris-Normandie that Le HAC were in advanced talks with Kombouaré, who has been out of work since leaving Paris FC over the summer. In recent years, he has garnered a reputation as a manager capable of guiding clubs away from relegation trouble. He did so at Paris FC before being replaced by Liam Rosenior in the summer. Le Havre are in need of a manager of his profile. The club currently sit bottom of Ligue 1 with just two points from their first nine games. That run of form cost Didier Digard his job. In the wake of that decision, seemingly taken by the owners, president Jean-Michel Roussier resigned, whilst sporting director Demba Ba has also opted to leave. Despite reports, Kombouaré has not been contacted about the managerial vacancy, RMC Sport understands. Jair Karam will be on the bench for this weekend’s game against FC Lorient. The teenager made history by becoming the club's second-youngest goalscorer in the Champions League, but his personal milestone was overshadowed by a late collapse against Fenerbahce. item.title: ‘We’ve been a perfect match’ — Harry Kane details relationship with Bayern Munich manager
item.description: (Photo by Kevin Voigt/GettyImages) | Getty Images Harry Kane has made it clear that his decision to extend his contract with Bayern Munich was about more than just the club, the city, or the opportunity to compete for major trophies. His relationship with Vincent Kompany has also played an important role in making Munich feel like the pe rfect place to continue his career. Interestingly, Kane revealed that Kompany never put pressure on him to sign a ne w deal. Instead, the two shared an open conversation about how things were going at Bayern, with the manager allowing the situatio n to develop naturally. Kane also highlighted the respect he has for Kompany’s coaching philosophy, particularly his insistence that every player , regardless of experience or reputation, must meet the same standards. Kane explained Kompany’s role in his decision to stay. “Vince and I haven’t really discussed the contract. Obviously, he was a player himself not that long ago, so he understands exactly what’s going through a player’s mind. Vince is the type of manager and coach who believes that if you don’t want to be here, then you shouldn’t be here. We believe we’re on the right track, and we believe we have a great team, but he never put any pressure on me,” Kane said (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ). “We had one conversation about four weeks ago, more of an open discussion about how things were going rather than about the contract itself. And I respect that a lot. I have a great deal of respect for the boss. I respect his values and the way he pushes everyone. It doesn’t matter how many games you’ve played, whether you’ve made 500 appearances or you’re a young player just coming through. “He expects the same standards in training and in matches. That’s my mentalit y too. That’s how I see things as well. So, in that respect, we think alike. And ev er since he arrived at the club, I think we’ve been a perfect match.” That last line is v ery telling. Kane and Kompany clearly share a similar mentality when it comes to professionalism, preparation, and expectations. Both want to com pete for the biggest trophies, and neither appears particularly interested in lowering standards for anyone. For Bayern, that relationship could be just as important as the contract extension itself. Keeping Kane through 2029 means retaining an elite striker, but it also means maintaining o ne of the central pieces of Kompany’s project. While this is understood by most, it is easy to fall into the trap of thinking that Parsons will immediately be in mid-season form the second he steps onto the field for the first time. He himself told reporters that will not be the case. “I had a full lateral and medial meniscus repair, including the ACL, so when people are walking at three weeks, I’m still not weight bearing, so my quad is fully dead,” Parsons said . “I didn’t get off crutches until seven to eight weeks. So if you count that two months, I’m exactly where a nine-month (recovery) is supposed to be. So that’s why everyone’s timelines are different. I had a lot of damage done to my leg, and I think it’s a miracle that I’m even standing here today and opening up my window this early. “Am I going to be the All-Pro Micah, the person that I once was, this year? Probably not until later. item.title: The one Portugal milestone Cristiano Ronaldo failed to reach as he announces retirement
item.description: Photo by Alexander Hassenstein/Getty Images Cristiano Ronaldo is arguably the greatest soccer player to ever play for Portugal and has helped the national team win three trophies during his 23-year career. Despite having helped the nation reach heights they were not used to reaching, Ronaldo fell short of one achievement, which he always wanted to achieve with Portugal, and that was making 250 appearances. As he announced his retirement today, Ronaldo walks away with 234 international appearances and 146 goals, the most by any player. The announcement comes just one month after he left the Portuguese football camp in September, following controversy with head coach Jorge Jesus. “To the Portuguese people, the day has come for me to hand back the number seven shirt of our national team,” Ronaldo said in an Instagram video. “Today the time has come to pass it on to the future. It was not an easy decision, because some decisions are not made with the mind alone – they are also made with the heart. A journey that began in August 2003 and changed my life forever has come to an end.” The Portuguese national team put out an official video on Instagram with a powerful caption that read: “A legacy that will live on forever. Thank you for everything, captain.” They also put out a statement to inform fans that a tribute was in the works for the legendary soccer player. “It is our firm and immense desire to organise, plan, participate and actively collaborate in what will always be a fitting tribute to Cristiano Ronaldo’s immense career, in which fans and the country can applaud and celebrate, once again, the player who has given us so much,” the statement read. Throughout his career, Ronaldo represented Portugal in six European Championships and won the competition once in 2016. He has also played in six World Cups and led the national team to the semi-finals in 2006. Ronaldo played in 178 competitive games and 56 friendlies throughout his career. 57 of his competitive appearances came in the World Cup and Euros. The 41-year-old has scored 25 goals in these games and helped his country become one of the leading nations in soccer. As he retires from international football, the country will now be without an icon who has carried the expectations of the Portuguese people for over two decades. Although many would say that his performances declined in the past few years, there was still an expectation of something big happening with him on the field. However, with the legend now having announced his retirement, the next generation of Portuguese talent will have to showcase that they are capable of taking the country to great heights. item.title: Rare freshman starter Tommy Tofi settling in along Oregon football OL
item.description: It's been a bumpy ride for Oregon football's first regular-season true freshman starter in the Dan Lanning era. From the onset, Tommy Tofi, at a massive 6-foot-6, 360 pounds, possessed the tools to succeed in his first year with the Ducks (5-3, 3-2 Big Ten). Still, Lanning and offensive line coach A'lique Terry rarely go to first-year players along the interior. The only other first-year player to start for the Ducks under Lanning was current starting center Iapani Laloulu, who started the 2023 Fiesta Bowl only because Jackson Powers-Johnson opted out of the game. This is rare territory for an Oregon offensive lineman ahead of the Ducks ' biggest game of the season versus Ohio State. "It’s all been like kinda crazy," Tofi said. "Trying out different positions from left to right and just finding my rhythm." Tofi was used sparingly over the first month of the season and struggled with his assignments at times when he did get on the field. The freshman hasn't had trouble moving opposing players and creating gaps when he finds the right body, but the key has been being assignment sound. Since the second half against Nebraska on Oct. 17, Tofi has firmly held on to the left guard spot along the offensive line. He started his first game the week after against Illinois and played his best game of the season versus Northwestern last week. He said playing between Laloulu at center and veteran tackle Fox Crader has been instrumental to his success, along with his fair share of "cuss-outs." "A lot of cuss-outs from (Laloulu), (Douglas Utu) and a lot of the players," Tofi said with a smile when asked about how he's developed. "When you have four first-rounders on that D-line, that’s what helps you prepare and gets you ready for the season. Being able to go head-up with Matayo (Uiagalelei), Bear (Alexander), A’Mauri (Washington), Teitum (Tuioti), iron sharpens iron. You get better and better every day." Tofi has been part of a much-improved offensive line group that has stuck with a consistent group for the first time this season after rotating through different lineups over the first month and a half of the season. Ultimately, Lanning still wants to see more "strain" and effort from Tofi when the situation requires it. "Tommy is a guy that we’ve had a lot of confidence in from the beginning," Lanning said. "He’s got really good strength, got the ability to move people, which is huge. Now it’s about finding that extra strain. Can I strain from every play? I feel like every week that’s gotten a little better for Tommy." Alec Dietz covers University of Oregon football and women’s basketball for The Register-Guard.
